title: Should I keep going?
author: jocoly
selftext:
Losing motivation. Seems like the first 90% of the game came in one evening. Since then it’s been like pulling teeth trying to nail the finer details and the models I use are now feeling clunky instead of magic.

I’m thinking about removing several (most) of the vehicle options in my game and just focusing on the fighter jet gameplay to ease the workload of balancing it all.

How do you balance spending time on adding/improving fun gameplay mechanics vs polishing what you have there already?

comments.author: LowerMiddleClassMan
comments.body:
This has a lot of potential and looks like it can be fun.

However, heavily iterating is part of it.  Fine tuning, balancing, UI, UX and playtesting.  Even having a programmatic mindset is important so you build in a scalable manner that doesn’t require a whole bunch of refactoring or substantially more rework if you want to add in more features later.

I think this game has a ton of potential.  I do question if you will stick with it or have the stamina to do so…because

 1) It’s nowhere near 90% there, and, 

2) The whole I basically got it 90% there in one evening and now it’s taking forever comment?  That reads a lot like I tried to one shot a game, and now I’m making small tweaks just to the prototype and don’t actually want to be a game dev.

replies.author: jocoly
replies.body:
Thanks; I needed to hear this. I think the answer lies in dialing back AI’s role in the workflow and learning the finer details myself so I can have the control I want.

And you’re right, the question is do I have the stamina/motivation to transition from ‘AI one-shot prototype’ to ‘actual game I developed and understand under the hood’ - I’ll dive in and try to learn more about it.

comments.author: magic6435
comments.body:
" Seems like the first 90% of the game came in one evening. Since then it’s been like pulling teeth trying to nail the finer details" 

Welcome to the world of game design! This is not a bug, it's a feature, and exactly how it works without AI as well. Yes, keep going. Try to finish something, even if it's not your end goal. This is exactly why all of the one-shot demos on this sub are useless, because it's what you're experiencing now where the parts that actually make a game good come from.

comments.author: Nineneji
comments.body: Keep at it!! It looks like you have a nice core concept. Maybe make it like a 1v8 online where 1 control the big boss and 8 players goal is to take it out. To me you have  a nice foundation built, now is the time to build on it polish comes later.

comments.body: Take this idea into blender, make modular building pieces that actually break like destruction physics, take it into godot, this could be cool but you gotta put more of an effort in

comments.author: TheCelestialBubble
comments.body:
Lmao, it wasn't 90%, it was the first 10% at best. The assets are the easier part. Do what you suggested, at least for now. Dial it back and focus one strand of the game.

For your actual question, this probs changes with game, but I'm making a sidescroller and I've spent months designing and iterating. I've eventually came to a strategy of planning a section, doing a first pass up to a certain segment, essentially a crude but mildly valiant attemot to get things in shape for a set of areas, then going back and doing a second pass with the new detail in my head. Fixing and changing things as I go. Seems to work quite well for me. I would never try and one shot the whole game... It adds more work cos you don't just build from scratch, you now have to fit everything in with your constraints.

comments.author: MickQn
comments.body:
Yeah, this screams of telling AI all your hopes and dreams and then praying that it works out 😀 been there... Haha dial it back. Just focus on one area at a time. I'm on the fourth rebuild of my game from scratch because of this same dilemma. I think it's what we all do when starting anything out. We don't think of the big picture with all the little details, we just see a beautiful big picture. It isn't until you start to dive in that your realize you don't know what you don't know and that's when you need to embrace the suck. Start grinding on reading material and asking more questions, build test benches so that you can focus on one specific aspect of your game, and try not to think about the full game for several months until all the other pieces are built. 

AI is going to lean towards it's biases unless you tell it otherwise. You need to work with it to focus on breaking those biases one feature at a time so that you have a game that you want and not something that you asked for and AI goes "I have just the copypasta for that right here".

replies.author: jocoly
replies.body: Facts, well said. I’ll break it down into smaller sections with more manageable goals. I’m going to resist the urge to shelve this for another idea - because that just starts the cycle all over again and I’ll be at the same place in \~2 weeks.
